gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much battery a 12 V split-phase inverter uses just sitting idle. The AIMS 4000 W 12 V split-phase unit that ChatGPT showed (Outbound Power, $1,949) is listed at 50 W idle. That is 50 W × 24 h ÷ 12.8 V ≈ 94 Ah a day, nearly a whole 100 Ah 12 V LiFePO4 battery gone with no load. Two Victron MultiPlus-II 12/3000 units, the pair needed for 240 V, use about 56 Ah a day (15 Ah in search mode).
standout_why: I compared against the cited Victron 'help me choose' page, which has no idle, current-draw or cost figures, and the cited Victron MultiPlus-II 2x120V product page, whose visible spec table lists power and weight but no zero-load power. In ChatGPT's results, Victron's datasheet or manual may carry the 15 W per-unit zero-load figure. But no rival turns it into Ah per day, doubles it for the two-unit split-phase setup, or gives any idle figure for the AIMS or Sun Gold Power units on ChatGPT's cards. ChatGPT's own answer gave only the ~370 A full-load draw.
decides: For an off-grid cabin or RV bank that stays on all day, idle draw matters more than the 4,000 W rating. On paper the AIMS unit costs nearly a 100 Ah battery a day at idle, so its 21 W power-saver mode (≈39 Ah a day) is required. The Victron pair is the lowest-idle way to get true 120/240 V (8 W in search mode ≈ 15 Ah a day), but it takes two units weighing 100 lb. Sun Gold Power is the cheapest at $0.23 per watt today, but its idle draw is unsourced, so the lowest-drain claim can't be checked for it. Also, its price today is $936, not the $624 ChatGPT showed.
